description: Knox used bash to attempt Mac filesystem operations during plaud-ingest step-01-discover. Bash runs in an isolated Linux sandbox and cannot access Mac paths (/Users/, ~/). The workflow aborted at step-01 because none of the Mac-side file reads or script executions succeeded. Root cause: no plaud-ingest workflow file or skill file explicitly stated that Desktop Commander must be used for Mac filesystem operations — Knox defaulted to bash.
correction: All Mac-side operations (running fetch_plaud.py, reading ~/.config/plaud/token.json, listing ~/Downloads/transcript-staging/) must use mcp__Desktop_Commander__start_process, mcp__Desktop_Commander__read_file, and mcp__Desktop_Commander__list_directory respectively. Chrome operations use mcp__Control_Chrome__* tools. Bash is sandbox-only.
systemic_fix: Added explicit MANDATORY EXECUTION RULE to workflow.md, step-01 through step-05, and all four plaud skill files (plaud-discover, plaud-transcripts, plaud-trigger, plaud-speaker-id) stating that Mac filesystem operations require Desktop Commander tools, not bash. Also updated all do-shell-script examples to show mcp__Desktop_Commander__start_process syntax. Watcher sub-agent spawn prompts updated to carry the rule into spawned agents.
